sections.description: This section focuses on the initial presentation of the patient, the physical examination findings, and the immediate steps taken to stabilize the patient and manage acute symptoms.
subtopics: Analyzing the triad of symptoms: Abdominal pain, dyspnoea, and pregnancy in the second trimester
Physical examination: Distinguishing between upper quadrant and pelvic abdominal masses
Immediate symptomatic management: The role of analgesia and semi-orthostatic positioning for diaphragmatic decompression
Baseline laboratory evaluation and identifying concurrent comorbidities (e.g., iron deficiency anaemia, urinary tract infection)

sections.description: This section explains the diagnostic modalities used to characterize the masses and the clinical reasoning used to differentiate between various pelvic and abdominal pathologies during pregnancy.
subtopics: Ultrasonography in pregnancy: Evaluating cystic vs. solid components and vascularity
The role of non-contrast MRI: Safety considerations and diagnostic accuracy for intramural and posterior leiomyomas
Interpreting CA-125 in pregnancy: Understanding physiological trends versus oncological markers
Differential diagnosis: Distinguishing decidualised endometriomas from cystic degenerating leiomyomas

sections.description: This section covers the criteria used to justify surgical intervention during the second trimester and the intraoperative logic for selective myomectomy.
subtopics: Indications for urgent myomectomy: Torsion, rupture, and severe symptomatic compression
Surgical approach: Rationale for laparotomy over laparoscopy in large, multiple, or critical-location masses
Intraoperative findings: Identifying the twisted pedunculated leiomyoma
Surgical strategy: Balancing mass removal with the preservation of the pregnancy (selective vs. total removal)

sections.description: This section details the medical management following surgery and the strategy for ensuring a safe pregnancy and delivery.
subtopics: Postoperative medical management: Treating iron deficiency anaemia and K. pneumoniae infection
Pregnancy maintenance: Use of prophylactic progesterone after uterine surgery
Monitoring fetal viability and growth in the context of residual uterine masses
Determining the mode of delivery: Rationale for elective Caesarean section due to obstructive pelvic masses

sections.section_title: Clinical Significance: Leiomyomas in the Gravid Uterus
sections.description: This section provides a broader pedagogical overview of the pathophysiology and management guidelines for uterine leiomyomas during pregnancy based on the case's findings.
subtopics: Natural history of leiomyoma size changes across the three trimesters
Risks associated with myomectomy during pregnancy: Bleeding, preterm labor, and uterine rupture
The impact of myoma location (submucosal, intramural, subserosal) on fetal head progression and delivery
The importance of a multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach in managing complex obstetric-surgical cases
